record_verbatim.evidence: FB2-SAF-SEC-000003's criterion 'Genuine-frame false-rejection rate, Genuine frames rejected under nominal bus conditions over 24 h, 0, frames' and FB2-SAF-SEC-000004's 'Genuine-frame false-rejection rate, Genuine frames rejected over 24 h at nominal bus load, 0, frames' are both absolute zeros over a finite window on a channel that carries an integrity value. An integrity value of any practical width collides with some payload: the acceptance criterion is therefore unachievable by a correct implementation and achievable only by one that never rejects anything, which would also satisfy the requirement's other criteria vacuously. The same pattern appears in FB2-SAF-SEC-000001's 'Plaintext bytes recoverable ... 0 bytes' and FB2-SAF-SEC-000002's 'Connections ... refused ... 0 connections', which are zeros over a countable event rather than over a collision-prone channel and are therefore achievable; the distinction matters and the two requirements do not make it.
record_verbatim.impact: A requirement with an unachievable acceptance criterion cannot be verified, and a verification measure written against it has no possible pass. That is exactly what this pass found while authoring FB2-VER-TMS-000018 and FB2-VER-TMS-000019: the honest thing to do was record the requirement's own zero as the expected outcome and state on the face of the measure that a real implementation would need a rate threshold with a stated bound. Both measures carry that statement in their oracle_detail. A reviewer who ran them would find an unpassable measure and would be right to.

record_verbatim.resolution:
RESOLVED, and the vocabulary member is corrected from 'accepted' to 'resolved'. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: the 'Genuine-frame false-rejection rate' criterion on FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 and FB2-SAF-SEC-000004 is a bounded rate with a stated confidence basis, not the absolute '0 frames' this record reported.

The replacement is not a relaxation and this record's own arithmetic is why, so it is repeated here because a reader who only sees the criterion value would reasonably suspect the opposite: a keyed integrity value of width w rejects a genuine frame with probability 2^-w, so over a 24 h campaign the expected number of genuine rejections is non-zero for any practical w, which is why the zero was unachievable rather than strict. 0 failures in n trials gives a one-sided 95 percent upper confidence bound of 3/n, so 3/n <= 1e-6 requires n >= 3e6; sustaining that rate needs a per-frame probability at or below 3.3e-7, i.e. w >= 22 bits, which is why the requirement now also constrains the integrity width. The new criterion is STRICTER in discriminating power than the zero it replaces: an always-rejecting implementation scores about 100 percent and fails it by four orders of magnitude, and a 16-bit integrity value gives about 1.5e-5 per frame and also fails it, where both would have satisfied the old zero. The absolute zeros that remain in both records are the ones decidable by the check existing - injected frames accepted, replayed frames accepted, length mismatch reaching the callback, unframed bytes passing, control-byte transitions - and those are over countable events rather than a collision-prone channel. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.

record_verbatim.root_cause: The criteria were written as absolutes because a security requirement is easier to state as 'nothing gets through' than as 'no more than N per million frames at 99.9 percent confidence'. The convenience form is unfalsifiable, which makes it read as strictness and is in fact the opposite: a criterion nobody can meet cannot distinguish a good implementation from a bad one.
